topic: Jellyfish Study: More AI Tokens ≠ Better Developer Productivity

key_points: Coined the term 'tokenmaxxing' — the race to consume more AI tokens than anyone else at your company
Jellyfish Q1 2026: 7,548 engineers studied — largest token users got 2x throughput at 10x the token cost
GitClear data: regular AI users experienced 9.4x higher code churn than non-AI counterparts
Meta ranked 85,000 employees on token consumption leaderboard — 'Token Legend' burned 281 billion tokens in 30 days
Uber exhausted entire annual AI budget ($3.4 billion) in four months
Bottom 20% token spend averaged 11 merged PRs per quarter; top 20% averaged 23 PRs
Typical user: ~51 million tokens/month; 90th percentile: ~380 million tokens/month (7x more)
Token volume has an efficiency curve — gains plateau and cost-per-PR climbs sharply at high end
The real opportunity is to optimize how tokens are used, not maximize them
Per-developer token consumption rose about 18.6x in nine months driven by agentic tools
Harvard Economics + Jellyfish: analyzed 100,000 software engineers across 500 companies
AI is making coding faster and code quality doesn't seem to be suffering at the individual level
No significant increase in features shipped despite measurable speed gains
No observable shift toward higher-value work at the organizational level
2026 is about figuring out ROI: where AI delivers real value vs. falls short
Jellyfish benchmark: 700+ companies, 200,000 engineers, 20 million PRs (March 2026)
64% of engineers believe they're achieving at least 25% productivity increase using AI
Code acceptance rates are 80-90% claimed but real-world acceptance drops to 10-30% after revisions
Engineers have to return to revise AI-generated code far more often than before
Rising awareness of costs is changing industry calculus on AI tool investment
Updated benchmark: 1,000+ companies, 200,000 engineers, 37 million PRs
Median AI adoption: 71%; median AI code ratio: 27%
Top AI adopters see 2x PR throughput vs low adopters
Autonomous agent PRs for top adopters now reach 35% of all PRs
5–11% increase in reverted code as AI usage increases — hidden quality cost

angles: The tokenmaxxing paradox: how measuring AI by token consumption became a productivity anti-pattern that misleads engineering leaders
The efficiency curve exposed: data shows where AI-driven gains peak (low-to-mid usage) and where cost-per-PR climbs unsustainably
The Harvard-Jellyfish disconnect: individual coding speed is up, but organizational features shipped and business impact are not
Hidden productivity killer: AI-assisted code churn is erasing many of the speed gains (861% churn increase under high AI adoption)
The AI adoption divide: top 10% of teams pulling far ahead while the median company lags — what the gap reveals
From token budgets to outcome budgets: how forward-thinking engineering leaders are restructuring AI ROI measurement
